newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Peter Guilford briefed on Monday and Tuesday's East-West seminar on anti-dumping to take place in the Renaissance Hotel. He said the aim of the seminar was to explain European anti-dumping policy, to hear the views of the Eastern and Central European countries officials and businessmen on this issue and to encourage discussion between Western and Eastern enterprises.

Guilford said participants would inlcude Commissioners Sir Leon Brittan and Hans van den Broek, Czech Minister for Trade and Industry Vladimir Dlouhy, Dutch Director General for Foreign Economic Relations Frans Engering, UNICE President Francois Perigot and WTO experts. Guilford also said there would be a news conference/open debate on Monday at 1140/1040 GMT.

Spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said Commissioner Manuel Marin would meet and address participants to the new exchange programme between EU and ASEAN entrepreneurs "JEM" at 1830/1730 GMT in the DG1B atrium. He said accredited journalists were welcome.

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission's policy on the accession of Central and Eastern European countries to the EU was not to refer to any dates. Van der Pas therefore deleted the statement that 'the first accessions is likely to be no earlier than 2002' in Wednesday's Commission memo.

Asked why press reviews were not made available to journalists any more, van der Pas said it was an internal issue. He also said the problem came from journalists taking the press reviews out of the Commission buildings, therefore creating a copyright issue. Van der Pas said the news clipping service would be maintained for journalists but not the press reviews until he received a joint declaration by newspapers and agencies that the Commission can use the articles for news reviews leaving the Commission buildings.
In answer to a question Guilford said Commissioner Brittan would hold a joint news conference with Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer on Wednesday at 1430/1330 GMT.
In answer to a question, spokesman Gerry Kiely said the Commission legal services were asked to examine a case against gelatine producers but that it was not a Commission priority for the moment.

- IP/97/49: Cambodia: Commission approves humanitarian aid worth ECU 1.5 million.
- IP/97/52: Statement by Neil Kinnock following the negotiation session between EU and Switzerland on land transport.
- Speech/97/14: Speech by Commissioner Van den Broek on the Czech Republic and the EU enlargement.
- Speech/97/15: Speech by Commissioner Flynn at the Conference ob social policy and economic performance.
- Speech/97/16: Speech by Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan to the Ernst & Young Dinner.
